caption: None of these showed up overnight. They crept in over a season of hard runs, long hauls, and sleeping standing up in a trailer. North Texas ropers — if you're blaming your horse's head and you've already tried three different trainers, it might be time to look at what's happening from the poll to the pelvis. Dr. Leo checks the spots that take the most load on a rope horse: the atlas, the lumbar, the sacroiliac. When those are off, your horse can't do what you're asking — no matter how much you school it. Book now — shortgochiro.com or call (406) 799-3369.

DFW barrel racers and ropers — if your horse runs hard, hauls long, and goes right back to work, their body is carrying more than you think. Dr. Leo sees it every week: horses that looked fine at the arena but stepped off the trailer a different animal. A post-haul adjustment isn't a luxury.
